tldr_label: TL;DR: Wall Street caps its best week since 2022, Russia pounds Ukraine's grid and rail as Trump calls victory over Iran 'at hand', and EU leaders leave Brussel

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: The Dow rose 592 points and the Nasdaq 2.3% on Black Friday. All three indexes gained more than 5% for the week, and Brent posted its first weekly rise in November ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting. [[TAG:success:best week]]

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: Russian strikes hit energy, rail and civilian sites in nine regions, killing seven at an enterprise in Nizhyn. Russia said Ukraine launched hundreds of drones at the Moscow region. [[TAG:danger:grid war]]

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: Trump told troops that victory over Iran is 'at hand' and offered Tehran a deal. Kuwait summoned Iran's ambassador after the deaths of two Italians, which Iran denies causing. [[TAG:warning:rhetoric]]

tldr_bullets.label: Europe
tldr_bullets.body: An EU summit ended without agreement on the 2028-2034 budget or a €45 billion Ukraine loan. Spain votes Sunday, and polls favor the right. [[TAG:warning:deadlock]]

tldr_bullets.label: Gaza
tldr_bullets.body: An Israeli strike killed two MSF staff outside a Gaza clinic. Israel said the men were Hamas members, and MSF said its site was clearly marked. [[TAG:danger:aid workers]]

sections.title: Markets: Best Week Since 2022
sections.summary: Dow adds 592 on Black Friday; indexes up over 5% on week; Brent rises before OPEC+

paragraphs.heading: Black Friday
paragraphs.body: Kiplinger reported the Dow added 592 points on Black Friday as AI fears faded. JBizNews reported the Dow up 1.18%, the S&P 500 up 1.6% and the Nasdaq up 2.31% in the shortened session. TradingView said US equities closed on top. BigGo Finance reported the Nasdaq gained 6.7% for the week, and reports said the Dow logged its biggest weekly advance since October 2022. [[TAG:success:rebound]]

paragraphs.heading: Oil and OPEC+
paragraphs.body: Forbes Middle East reported Brent gained 3% for its first weekly rise in November ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting. Trading and Investment News said Brent was near $97 before the 2027 quota talks, while FinanceFeeds put Thursday's level at $95.58. Reports said producers are expected to keep targets unchanged for the first quarter of 2027. [[TAG:info:OPEC+ Sunday]]

sections.title: Ukraine: Grid and Rail Hit
sections.summary: Strikes hit nine regions and kill seven in Nizhyn; Moscow reports mass drone attack

paragraphs.heading: Russian Strikes
paragraphs.body: Euronews reported Russian drone strikes hit Ukraine's energy, rail and civilian infrastructure in nine regions, causing deaths. Ukrinform and h.ua reported seven people were killed at an enterprise in Nizhyn as the rescue operation concluded. NewsLantern reported Zelensky said Russia launched more than 400 drones and 40 missiles, while the Boston Report, citing Ukraine's Air Force, put one overnight wave at 162 drones. The figures may cover different time windows. Zelensky had warned of the attack a day earlier, Manila Times reported, carrying AP. [[TAG:danger:energy]]

paragraphs.heading: Cross-Border
paragraphs.body: The Boston Report said Moscow's mayor reported 460 drones targeting the region overnight into Saturday. This is an unverified Russian claim. The Japan Times reported a Russian naval flotilla bound for Libya turned around after the sinking of a warship there. [[TAG:warning:claims]]

sections.title: Iran: 'Victory at Hand'
sections.summary: Trump tells troops victory is near and offers a deal; Kuwait summons Iran's envoy

paragraphs.heading: Trump's Message
paragraphs.body: WMAL, ANI and Middle East Eye reported Trump told troops on Thanksgiving that victory over Iran is at hand, that Tehran will never have a nuclear weapon, and that Iran has every chance to make a deal. ByteWire reported he warned of a strike on Pickaxe Mountain, a suspected enrichment site. He did not formally declare the war over. [[TAG:warning:rhetoric]]

paragraphs.heading: Kuwait and Hormuz
paragraphs.body: Gulf News reported Iran offered to join a probe of the Kuwait drone attack that killed two Italian technicians. Latin Times and HNGN reported Iran denies responsibility. Reports said Kuwait summoned Iran's ambassador. The Tribune reported Iranian MP Esmaeil Kowsari claimed Iran has full control of the Strait of Hormuz and will break the US blockade; Washington has disputed such claims. [[TAG:danger:Gulf]]

sections.title: Europe: Summit Fails, Spain Votes
sections.summary: No deal on EU budget or €45bn Ukraine loan; Spain votes Sunday with right favored

paragraphs.heading: Brussels
paragraphs.body: Euronews reported the EU budget summit collapsed, and The Intelligent reported leaders left Brussels without agreement on the long-term budget or a Ukraine loan. AOL called it a summit that ended in disarray as leaders clung to red lines. Euronews' live coverage said Macron threatened to end budget talks if there is no deal in December. Talks were pushed to the December summit. [[TAG:warning:deadlock]]

paragraphs.heading: Spain
paragraphs.body: The Rio Times reported Spain votes Sunday in an early general election, with polls favoring the conservatives. Seat projections for the People's Party and Vox vary by poll. [[TAG:info:Sunday vote]]

sections.title: Israel: Eight-Day Pledge
sections.summary: Eisenkot accuses Likud of stalling, vows government within eight days

paragraphs.heading: Coalition
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported Eisenkot accused Netanyahu's Likud of stalling coalition talks to force new elections, and Anadolu reported he vowed to form a government within eight days. The Jewish Chronicle and Manila Times reported his coalition deal with Yair Golan's Democrats. Reported seat totals for his bloc vary, from about 36 to 48 depending on which partners are counted, all well short of 61. A separate Al Jazeera analysis examined Eisenkot testing a power-sharing arrangement with Netanyahu. [[TAG:info:short of 61]]

sections.title: Gaza: MSF Staff Killed
sections.summary: Israeli strike kills two MSF guards outside clinic; Israel says they were Hamas

paragraphs.heading: The Strike
paragraphs.body: The National, RTE and US News, carrying Reuters, reported an Israeli strike killed two MSF staff outside a Gaza clinic. MSF said it was outraged and that its premises were clearly marked and known to the Israeli military. ABC Australia reported Israel said the men were Hamas members posing as aid workers, which MSF disputes, and Israel did not provide evidence. [[TAG:danger:disputed]]

paragraphs.heading: Other Strikes
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported Israeli attacks killed four people in Gaza as a son of Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya survived a strike targeting his family. [[TAG:warning:truce strained]]

sections.title: Asia and Africa
sections.summary: Taiwan local elections split early; Seoul watches for Kim trip; Badme fighting

paragraphs.heading: Taiwan
paragraphs.body: The Japan Times described Taiwan's local elections as tight and watched by Beijing, and Dhaka Tribune reported polls closed Saturday. SCMP and Focus Taiwan reported early KMT wins in Kinmen and Lienchiang, while Kaohsiung Times reported the DPP keeping Kaohsiung. Results were preliminary at the time of reporting. [[TAG:info:early count]]

paragraphs.heading: Korea and the Horn
paragraphs.body: The Japan Times reported Seoul is monitoring signs of a possible visit to China by North Korea's Kim Jong Un. News Minimalist reported clashes between Ethiopian and Eritrean forces near the border town of Badme. [[TAG:warning:watch]]
